data.name: Stanwood
data.gender_notes: Stanwood is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English, Stanwood is composed of two elements: stan, meaning 'stone,' and wudu, meaning 'wood.' This name can be interpreted as 'strong and sturdy as a stone, yet adaptable and thriving like a tree.'. The name Stanwood carries the meaning “Stone and wood” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Stanwood usually hope their child will grow to embody stone and wood and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of strength, resilience, and adaptability.
data.etymology: Stanwood belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Stone and wood.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Stanwood total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Stanwood carries a sense of strength, perseverance, and resilience. Its Old English origins reflect a connection to the natural world, emphasizing the durability of both stones and trees. This name has been carried by several places, Victorian era celebrities, and even in business entities. It embodies the enduring spirit which resonates with many individuals in their personal and professional lives.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Stanwood implies being rooted and grounded in both faith and life, drawing strength and nourishment from the Solid Rock of God and the faith He inspires within us. It's a reminder that our spiritual journey is similar to a growing tree that adapts, learns, and thrives despite challenges, staying firm in its faith and steadfast in its beliefs. Within its own name, Stanwood encourages us to be strong in spirit and persistent in our pursuit of a deeper connection with our Creator.
